label: When does an infinite regress weaken the case for this foundation’s possible absence?
summary:
See docs/notes/contingency-receptivity-c2.md#what-does-possible-absence-have-in-common-with-an-infinite-regress. Copying can explain each transmission while leaving the choice of content open. A third lossy relay under an independently known bound rules out all distant supply of the measured unit. Lossless transfer leaves the amount open, while identified distributed inputs determine the output of an endless lossy chain. A giver cannot produce the actuality it presupposes for its own action, but another giver can supply it. A memberwise infinitist can explain each receipt on those terms. No collective prohibition or quantitative bound for existential giving is established. An endless series of referrals that presuppose the next omission's warrant supports no initial omission on its own. Infinitary support can succeed with information-rich conditional constraints. A determining explanation of n's actual existence cannot use solely reasons also obtaining without n. A contingent distinguishing reason would need independent content and explanatory priority compatible with underivedness. A nonnecessitating account or a primitive stopping point can reject the determining requirement. The no-ground stipulation is about P at actuality. Avicenna's specification argument motivates two tests. A sufficient reason must discriminate the outcome and have the right explanatory direction. The casting case shows why those tests work when production is independently known. Their success leaves open both whether every contingent concrete existence has a determining reason and whether every complete, possibly joint reason must involve a form of dependence excluded for this unreceived act. A contingent intrinsic reason or noncausal external ground requires a substantive exclusion in the relevant reading of underivedness. The existing same-root proof needs the contingent-grounding bridge, and ruling out two-way possibility from here allows possible existence to yield necessity directly. For transport from a witness world that already requires existence, that world's access to all relevant alternatives suffices. The existing proof obtains a necessary witness from possible existence and the boxed necessity-if-existent principle. The section on exceptions compares eligibility for uncaused or ungrounded existence with evidence for an actual foundation. A permission granted on a shared feature removes that particular veto for a personal or impersonal rival. The echo and initial-boundary tests give positive reasons for local restrictions; neither establishes fundamental independence. High confidence in the specific explanatory failures and moderate confidence in suspension about bare P. No new theorem or formal premise change.

Retrospective proof-coverage audit, issue #2103 slice 1. Analyst formulations with attribution deferred. (a) ContingencyGrounding.firstMoverNecessaryByReceptivityOrPriorCause (result e5d49f99, argument f644aee8) concludes f9208664 from C2 (6508c239), the First Way witness, firstness, unreceivedness, MoversExistAt F w (hExist), ExcludedMiddle (hEM), and FirstUnmovedMoverIsPureAct (hPure). The proof obtains the witness’s actual existence from hExist and its moving relation. At each accessible world it uses hEM and rules out the absence case using C2, firstness and unreceivedness. The pure-act conjunct is supplied directly by hPure. Its encodings of contingency, existential receptivity and prior esse-causing are 97f37f5c, f9f58df7 and 211a6432 with the priority definitions on the argument. The proof excludes contingency by separately excluding each C2 disjunct at the same mover. (a) RegressSchema.regressSchemaPackage (74e00870) and the quantitative zero and vanishing-tail results (a6e858eb, 54e36212) give conditional obstructions in their own domains. QuantitativeTransferPaths.finitePath (082838e6, argument 28dc7b26) proves positive finite input reachability. Its internal geometric estimate assumes no reachable positive input. (d) The concrete three-relay example in #1908 allows a reachable active supplier immediately upstream of the passive block. It has no separate result ID. The missing finite-cutoff interface bounds that upstream output by 4, imposes three successive half-transfer inequalities inside the block with no local additions there, and bounds the terminal output by 1/2 while allowing positive input at the upstream boundary. (e) The analogy that an endless chain of existential giving cannot cover a retained creature in an order omitting this very n has no same-sense typed bridge from any of these quantitative hypotheses. A memberwise infinitist with local reasons, a basic whole and a different underived giver survive the analogy. Their de re admissibility and warrant remain open.
blocker:
No independently grounded restriction identifies n as the only possible provider of received existence across all inhabited orders, and a concrete-empty alternative contains no supply chain. Underivedness rules out producing n by a lottery or agent, but does not imply that all explanations must determine their outcomes. The available rearrangements and references do not certify an independently admissible alternative incompatible with n. A new test would identify a substantive constraint on all remaining givers or an independently motivated rule that licenses a de re omission while remaining evidence for a primitive P rather than its full ground at actuality.

Next distinct audit test. Require a candidate n-free inhabited order to state the retained creature, the complete purported donor roles and what it takes for each actual receipt to be supplied. Test that account against the existing inductive borrowing obstruction only if the roles are all derivative in its sense. To type the relay comparison, use a boundary output bound and passivity of just the inspected finite block. To apply it to the existential respect, warrant counterparts of that bound and those transfer inequalities.
